prompt:
Extract and normalize the one contact record embedded in the user's note. Return one bare JSON object with exactly name, phone, email, company, country as keys, each with a string or JSON null. Do not output prose, Markdown, questions, or extra keys.

1. Isolate the record. Its lines have labels and values separated by colon, equals, or tab, with variable labels and line order. The surrounding note and signatures are never sources. Do not derive values from an email domain or a company suffix; use suffixes only to recognize and clean company values. Trim each value and collapse whitespace runs to single spaces. Absent values, empty values and placeholders (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD; any case) are null, subject only to the international-phone country fallback below.

2. Assign before formatting. A record value containing @ is email. A record value with at least seven digits and no characters other than digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after removing a leading tel: and an extension is phone, regardless of label. Recognized extensions include ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12, extension 12. If the name-labeled value ends in a legal suffix and the company-labeled value does not, swap the two. Legal suffixes, case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. The only explicit country source is the country line.

3. Resolve country and phone together. Normalize the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 using English, Swedish or German country names, alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes (any case), and common aliases including UK or Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA or U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ. After dropping tel: and the extension, skip an opening parenthesis when testing for a leading + or 00. Either prefix makes the phone international. Delete any (0) before stripping parentheses and the other formatting characters (spaces, dashes, dots and slashes); on the resulting compact number, replace a leading 00 with +. Keep the number's own calling code even if it disagrees with the country line. If the country line is absent, empty or a placeholder, fill country from the international calling code only if the code belongs to one country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. This is the only override to missing-value handling. If the phone is national, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the normalized country's calling code. Without a country, output null for a national phone. All non-null phones have E.164 form: plus followed only by calling code and national significant number digits.

4. Format the text fields. Name: reorder Last, First by splitting at the first comma; remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof with optional dot, any case; uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest in each space- or hyphen-separated part. Company: remove a trailing listed suffix including an optional preceding comma; uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. Email: remove a mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets and lowercase the entire address. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate. Unicode strings are compared under NFC.

5. Before emitting the object, check that every assigned, usable value was normalized rather than dropped. Do not guess missing values or use empty strings in place of null.
